\mxnewpage\section*{Solutions EV4-A}\label{EV4-A-CORR}
\textbf{MCQ:} 1 C, 2 C, 3 D, 4 C, 5 A, 6 A, 7 C, 8 B, 9 A, 10 A, 11 B, 12 A. Each correct answer: 0.5 point; total 6.
\paragraph{Checks of the fluency questions.} Order of operations; sum of fractions; subtraction of exponents; multiplying coefficient 1.2; division by 0.8; product 1.25 times 0.8; solving an affine equation; vertical increment divided by horizontal; mean; angle divided by 360; complement to 1; substitution in brackets.
\subsection*{Exercise 1 -- Two linked variables}
\begin{enumerate}
\item Both expectations equal 2. \textit{Marking: 1 point. Result and basic justification expected; half a point possible for a correct but unfinished approach.}
\item $E(X^2)=\dfrac{14}{3}$, so $V(X)=\dfrac{2}{3}$; same variance for Y. X+Y=4, variance 0. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\item $0\ne \dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{2}{3}$. The counterexample is on a single sample space; Y depends on X. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\end{enumerate}
\subsection*{Exercise 2 -- Comparing a curve and a line}
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h\prime=1-e^{-x}$. \textit{Marking: 1 point. Result and basic justification expected; half a point possible for a correct but unfinished approach.}
\item Negative if x<0, positive if x>0; minimum h(0)=0. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\item Approximation 0.98; from below, thanks to the inequality. \textit{Marking: 2 points. Method or justification: 1; calculation and conclusion: 1.}
\end{enumerate}
